verdicts.reasoning: I measured the raw fixed-7 frame. In the horn box, 2.5 % of pixels are above L* 5 and the median C* is 0.0. Lemon pixels (C* >= 20, L* > 10) are 0.1 % of the niche opening (1010,25)-(1325,262). I looked at it at 1:1 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b64/judge-owner-verify/v-horn-1to1-all.png): the horn is a black glass slab with a thin rim, and the driver is only a faint dark disc. At 800 (v-speaker-800-x2.png, same folder) the driver does not show at all, and the Tropos reads as a lemon cabinet with a black slab on top. At 168 (v-thumbs-x5.png) the top is a black rectangle and the horn is gone. Nothing in the frame read as CG to me.

I measured single rows on the raw crops. The lemon starts at x 1138-1141 in w1 and w2, x 1145-1148 in a1 and a3, and x 1142-1145 in b. In a and w the jump from L* about 0 to 23-45 takes 1-2 px. Dimming does not move or soften it: w1 and w2 share the same x and the same 1-2 px rise, and so do a1 and a3. The fill is flat: 16 px block medians in w2's lemon area are 32-36 over most of it, 26-29 near the right rim and 21-26 at the bottom, with no shading from rim to throat. The rim is unbroken in every option. One correction: b's edges are not 15/4/3 and 8/2/3 px wide. Five-row profiles at rows 140, 180 and 215 rise in 2-4 px (b160 0>1>14>21, 0>5>21, 1>6>13>25>35; b400 1>5>27>36, 1>15>35, 4>11>20>38>48), as hard as a and w, so the judge's method miscounted them. F2 does not give the cause, and I found it: the edge is the left end of the lit back seen straight through the clear horn. The w1 shot puts the panel's left edge at x 7.93, y 6.02, which projects to x 1141. Straight camera rays switch from the left side wall to the back at x 1141.5 in every row. The pale band under the horn ends at that same x (1141 in w2, 1148 in a3; v-band-x3.png). a's panel starts 2 cm further right, and its edge sits 7 px further right, against 7.2 px projected.

In my 3x crops (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b64/judge-owner-verify/v-streak-x3-b-w.png), b160 and b400 have thin, straight, bright yellow lines running from the lower-left rim toward the driver. One runs about (1105,245)-(1167,213), with a fainter one below it, and b400's are stronger. w1 and w2 have none, and a1 and a3 have none either (v-niche-1to1.png). The line still shows at 800 (v-speaker-800-x2.png). In b, the niche's top and the upper part of its left wall are lit grey and fade downward, so it reads as a lit display box; b400 reads most like a grey box. The band under the horn measures L* 0.5 in b160 and 1.6 in b400, and the posts do not show. Whether the lines read as a crack or as a reflection glint is a judgment; to me they read as a glint or a scratch line.

The panel strip (1302-1320, 90-220) reproduces: a1 L* 53.4, b* -9.6; a3 L* 69.5, b* -9.0. It looks blue-grey at 1:1 and at 800. The judge's range for the frame's whites leaves one out: sleeve stripes +1.7, record label +1.0, lamp undersides +0.4, but the triangle sign's white is -0.7. That is in the judge's own whites.py, and a is still far bluer than all of them. At 800, a1 against w1 differs by a mean of 0.16 levels, all of it inside the horn and panel (800 px x 566-661, y 21-143), so it is otherwise the same picture. Two sub-claims depend on which part of the cabinet you compare. 'Greener': h 103.6 and 104.8 against the cabinet-box median 97.3, but only 3-4 degrees against the cabinet's top band directly below (h 100.7), and I cannot see it. 'Lighter than its cabinet': a3's horn (41.8) is lighter than the cabinet median (32.3) but darker than that top band (52.9).

The readings reproduce: w1 22.2 / 31.1 / 98.3 and b160 24.4 / 33.4 / 95.0. Both lit halves are darker than every lemon part of their cabinet. That includes the cabinet's clear lemon ring around the woofer, which I measured at L* 28.5, C* 31.0, h 94.1 in every option. They are much darker than the top band directly below the horn (L* 53.0), which is about 55 % darker, not a quarter to a third. At 800 (v-speaker-800-x2.png) both horns read as dark olive. The studio part depends on which box you use. The studio horn (plain patch L* 66.8) is lighter than the judge's whole cabinet-front box (61.2) and the side (45.8), but darker than the cabinet's top band (92.3).

Every number reproduces: horn 32.6 / 41.2 / 99.1, strip 61.1 against 51.0, band 38.5 against 28.8, pale share 10.5 % against 10.3 %, strip b* -4.3. Edges are clean with no streaks, the posts show in silhouette, and at 800 the strip reads as a pale panel, not glare. The doubtful part is 'matches its cabinet in lightness'. That holds only for the median over the whole cabinet face, which spans L* 19.6-55.4 from p10 to p90. The top band directly under the horn reads 53.0 / 40.7 / 100.7: w2's horn has the same chroma and hue but is 20 L* darker. It is 4 L* lighter than the clear woofer ring (28.5). At 1:1 and 800 I see a lemon horn a shade darker and more olive than the cabinet's pale top. The studio horn also sits below its top band (66.8 against 92.3), so the relation is similar but not the same. As a ratio to the top band, w2 is 0.61 against the studio's 0.72, and a3 (0.79) and b400 (0.75) come closer.

The pale shares reproduce exactly (a1 10.4, a3 10.7, b160 6.4, b400 10.2, w1 10.3, w2 10.5, fixed-7 2.0 %). The a3 and w1 shot files differ only in props[23], a single panel at x 8.25, so a and w light only the near bay. In fixed-7 the far niche is black above the far Tropos (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b64/judge-owner-verify/v-farbay-x2.png). In a and w the panel shows as a rectangle: the strip's hard top edge at y about 70 is the panel's own top edge, which projects to y 72. It reads as a backlit back panel, and b reads as a lit box (v-niche-1to1.png). I could not check that b lights only the near bay, because there is no b shot file.

At 168 the horn is 29.2 x 20.9 px. At 1:1 and at 5x (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b64/judge-owner-verify/v-thumbs-x5.png), every backlit option shows a lemon square with a dark disc, fixed-7 shows a black top, and live shows a shaded gold wedge. Only live's reads as a flared shape. The site thumbnail differs from a 168 x 94 Lanczos downscale of the site's 1600 webp by 3.50 levels on average, and from one of live.png by 4.03.

My own pixel-difference search puts all six crops at (960,0): 1.07-1.18 mean difference on the shelving, against 1.84 or more one pixel off. The crop's edge bands differ from fixed-7 by 1.9-3.0 mean (95th percentile 6-9), the right shelving by 0.86-0.93, and whole-frame L* is 17.42-17.79 against 17.07. No seam shows at 800, even with a hard paste (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b64/judge-owner-verify/v-seam-800-x2.png). My 24 px-feather composites differ from the judge's by 0.01 mean at 800. The light honesty of w2's panel has indeed not been audited.

verified.recommendation_check:
I agree with putting a real full-frame w2 render beside fixed-7. Of the six tests, w2 is the brightest with no streaks, no lit box and no blue panel. Its horn reads lemon, while w1 and b160 read dark olive: their horns (L* 22-24) are darker even than the cabinet's clear woofer ring (28.5).

What I would change:

1. Drop "the only backlit option where the horn's lemon matches its own cabinet, as it does in the approved studio front". It rests on the median over the whole cabinet face (L* 19.6-55.4 from p10 to p90). The top band directly under the horn reads 53.0 / 40.7 / 100.7. w2's lit half has the same chroma and hue but is 20 L* darker, and at 1:1 and 800 I see it a shade darker and more olive. The studio horn is also darker than its top band (66.8 against 92.3). As a ratio to the top band, a3 (0.79) and b400 (0.75) come closer to the studio's 0.72 than w2 (0.61). Say instead that the horn reads as the cabinet's lemon, a shade darker than its pale top, as in the studio front.

2. Say why the horn is two-tone. The edge at x about 1140 is the left end of the lit niche back seen straight through the clear horn. Straight camera rays switch from the black left side wall to the back at x 1141.5. The pale band under the horn ends at the same x (1141). a's panel, whose edge is 2 cm further right, moves the edge 7 px right, as projected (7.2 px). So the left half faces the niche's black side wall. That is real, not a render fault, and no back light can change it. Only a lit or pale left wall could, and none of the six tests tried that.

3. The sentence claims "lit only by lights a real bar could have" for w2, which nobody has audited (F9). Read the full w2 render's emitter and shadow-ray reports first; its shot file asks for both. Keep the clause only if they come back clean, as fixed-7's audit did.

4. Small fixes:
- "the b options look cracked" should become "the b options show thin bright lines across the dark half that can read as scratches".
- F2's b edge widths are a measuring error: the b edges rise in 2-4 px, as hard as a and w.
- F4's whites leave out the triangle sign at b* -0.7.

The sentence I would send, once the audit is clean: "Both are lit only by lights a real bar could have. In the first, the clear lemon horn looks black because black felt is behind it. In the second, a soft light panel on the back of the niche shows the right half of the horn in the cabinet's lemon, a shade darker. The left half still looks black because it faces the niche's black side wall, and the pale panel shows beside and under the horn."

found.summary:
From the B1 seat the clear horn acts like a lemon-tinted window. I traced 18 camera rays through product.py's air path, with a formed wall about 6 to 8.5 mm thick. Each one crosses a single wall (its two faces, about 4 % reflected at each, no total internal reflection) and lands within about 1 cm of where a straight line would.
- Rays through the left part land on the niche's left cheek felt.
- Rays through the top band land on the niche ceiling felt.
- Only the right-centre part sees the back.

I built a geometric zone map from the camera model and a niche fitted to the w1 crop. It was not fitted to the horn's colours, and it predicts the lemon and black split in all six tests: the back zone is 97-100 % above L* 5 in every lit test, the cheek zone 4-11 %, the ceiling zone 0-2 %. Pixel-weighted, the horn's mouth from this seat shows:
- back 33 %
- left cheek 33 %
- ceiling 15 %
- pod 18 %

So no light on the back can make more than about a third of the horn lemon. None of the lane's tests changed the cheek or the ceiling.

Only two real routes make nearly the whole horn lemon:
- **(i) Light the whole bay.** Give the cheeks and ceiling a pale finish lit by the lane's strip. The bay becomes a lit box, the strongest display-case look of any option.
- **(iii) Move to a near-frontal seat.** About 0.85 m left and 0.6 m back from the B1 seat, at 21 mm. That is a different picture.

(ii) A light on the cheek fails: the horn looks straight at that spot, so the fixture shows through it as a hot spot.

(iv) Moving the speaker 2 cm right and 5 cm deeper in its bay takes the back zone from 33 % to 44 % with no new light. It is a free improvement to the lane's option (1), not a whole horn.

findings.about: Option (i): pale cheek and ceiling lit by the same concealed strip
findings.what:
This is the only route to a nearly whole lemon horn in the approved composition.

Estimated from a line-source model of the strip under the top lip (my geometry, not a render):
- **Cheek zone** (seen through the horn): 0.4-1.2x the light on the back behind the horn. Expected L* about 14-27, lemon, brighter top-front, darker lower-rear.
- **Ceiling zone**: about 0.02x direct light, so bounce only. The top band stays dim olive.
- **Lemon share**: the horn's share above L* 5 should go from about 32 % to about 70-75%. The pod stays dark.

Cost: the cheek's front strip beside the speaker (23k px, seen directly) gets 9.6x the back's light at z 2.48, 3.2x at 2.40, 1.0x at 2.20, 0.24x at 1.80 and 0.06x at 1.20. That gives a near-white band at the top left of the bay, fading down beside the cabinet. The lit area seen directly in the bay grows about 5x (9k to about 49k px). It is the strongest display-case read of any option.

A variant that lights only the rear of the cheek and ceiling (an opal 'lantern') adds only about 6k px of visible glow. But that glow hugs the horn's top and left rims like a halo, so I would expect it to read as lit for the camera.

A walnut or warm lining would show amber through the lemon horn, which misstates its colour.

verdicts.reasoning:
I built my own camera from render.py (a level camera with shift_y). It puts the horn rim and the cabinet's top edge on the w1 crop (ov-w1.png), and gradient correlation with fixed7.png confirms the crop origin (960, 0). The judge's niche front edges match the walnut/felt boundaries. Back at y 6.03 fits the ceiling-back edge right of the horn better than 6.08 (ov2-b400.png).

I wrote my own refraction trace through the shell as horn.py builds it: 6 mm offset, rim growing to 10 mm, smooth max with the 100 mm pod, so the neck is solid. In w1, a3, b160 and b400 the lemon/black boundaries sit on the traced back/cheek line and back/ceiling line (zones-mine-on-tests.png).

Through the cheek zone:
- incidence: median 23 deg (p2 7, p98 77)
- R: median 3.9 %
- exit: median 15 deg, max 40; no TIR
- landing: left cheek at y 5.60-6.02, z 2.09-2.52
- first-face mirror rays: 82 % leave through the mouth into the room (rightward and up), 4 % hit the cabinet top

The top band is 14-15 % of the mouth and lands on the ceiling at y 5.76-6.03. With straight-line zones I reproduce the judge's readings exactly:
- back: a1 23.7/32.9 ... w2 32.6/41.2, 96-100 % lit
- cheek: 4-10 % lit
- ceiling: 0-1 % lit

The strongest evidence is one the judge did not use. The strip in b160/b400 lights the felt cheek, and the horn's left part responds:
- cheek-zone p90 L*: 0.5 (w1), 3.1 (b160), 7.2 (b400)
- lit share: 5, 9, 11 %
- lit hue: 103
In horn-gamma-4.png, b400's left part shows dim olive.

Two small corrections:
- horn.py offsets the 6 mm wall within each section, so the path in resin is about 4.5-8 mm (median 4.9), not 6.6-8.5.
- Reflection is not absent. Along the bottom-left rim the incidence is near grazing (R up to about 30 %), and that makes the gold streaks in b160/b400 (streaks-vs-grazing.png).

Neither correction changes the finding.

My own straight-line map gives 42,335 mouth px:
- back 33.5 %
- cheek 33.1 %
- ceiling 15.3 %
- pod 18.1 %
- right cheek 0 % (0.3 % with refraction)

The tops-out claim holds. In the share of the mouth above L* 5:
- a1 to a3 (3x the strength): 34.6 to 36.5 %
- w1 to w2: 34.9 to 36.0 %

I reproduce the lane's box shares (w1 32.2, w2 33.3). But the box has about 7 % lit pixels outside the mouth (the panel beside the horn and the rim), so 'matches' is loose. The mouth's own lit share is 35-36 %, and its lemon share (C* >= 20, hue 85-115) is 30-32 %.

front-acid.png does show the driver pod as a dark disc on the real product.

Direct counts (mine against the judge's):
- cheek: 25.6k against 26.5k
- ceiling: 17.4k against 16.8k
- back: 6.3k against 9.0k. The judge's vis.py does not treat the horn's outer shell as an occluder.

The mechanism is plausible and partly seen: in b400 the strip-lit felt already shows through the horn as dim lemon.

But the judge's strip model does not match the rendered strip. On the directly seen felt cheek's front strip, b400 reads:
- L* 9.2 at z 2.48
- 14.3 at z 2.40
- 7.0 at z 2.30
- 2.4 at z 2.20
- 0.8 at z 2.0
- 0.3 (w1's level) at z 1.8 and below

b160 has the same shape. So the render peaks at about z 2.40, with a darker band right under the lip. The model peaks at z 2.48 (9.6x, against 3.2x at 2.40). The AgX toe stops me checking the lower ratios (0.24x, 0.06x).

So the cheek zone at 0.4-1.2x the back, L* 14-27, and 70-75 % are unverified guesses. 70-75 % above L* 5 is also more than back plus cheek (66.6 %), so it relies on the ceiling band, which the judge calls dim, crossing L* 5: dim olive counted as lemon.

'Only route' is too strong. The judge's own lantern variant is another route, and a pale lining lit by the back panel itself is untested.

The 49k px lit-area arithmetic checks: 6.3k + 25.6k + 17.4k.

My trace lands the cheek zone on the cheek at y 5.60-6.02, z 2.09-2.52, the area the judge names. A fixture there would be seen straight through the horn's left part.

The points about a lower mount (hidden behind the cabinet or showing through it, scalloping the cheek) are judgment. I did not measure them.

I reproduce the mouth-plane shares (back/cheek/ceiling/pod, %):
- now: 30.5/39.3/14.4/15.8
- eye 1.55: 33.7/40.3/8.5/17.5
- 0.4 m left: 48.8/24.6/10.4/16.2
- 0.6 m left: 56.1/17.0/11.3/15.6 (the judge has 59/16/9/16)
- frontal seat: 77.7/3.9/2.0/16.4 (pixel-weighted 78.4/3.1/2.0/16.5)

The framing checks out:
- 4.4 deg off axis against 27.6
- speaker silhouette 242 px against 342
- at the frontal seat the drinks (X 1000 and 1186), Cores, pendants and far bay project inside the frame
- at 0.4 m left with the same target, pendant 1 and a Core sit at the left edge, and Mantle and the drinks fall below the frame

I did not check that Mantle is cut at the frontal seat; I don't have its size.

One nuance: the angle alone is not enough. From (8.25, 3.5, 1.55), straight on but on the bar's seat line, the ceiling band stays at about 13 %. The step back to y 2.9 is what drops it to 1.7 %.

My own code reproduces the main claims:
- 2 cm right, 5 cm back: back 44.4, cheek 25.8, ceiling 11.5, pod 18.3 %
- felt gap left of the cabinet: 33.5 to 54 px
- with the 1.55 m eye and target z 1.635: 47.8/26.4/5.7
- toe-in 15 deg: 7.5 mm clearance each side, front-left corner 1.4 cm proud of the surround
- bay limits: x 7.64 and z 2.62

One correction: the 1.55 m eye drops the drinks about 44-48 px, not about 30. Their bases go to Y 908-923, outside the 900 px frame.

One benefit the finding does not state: the nudge halves the lit panel seen directly beside the horn (6.05k to 2.87k px). The directly seen felt cheek grows from 25.6k to 37.4k px.

The fact holds: props[23] is the only niche panel in the w1 shot.

The claimed look does not hold for B1:
- The far bay's back corners project at X 574-665, behind the opening's right edge at X 535 (the bay's right walnut upright). Inside the opening (X 451-535) you see only the far left cheek's felt, the far speaker and its horn (farbay-fixed7.png).
- Seen 62 deg off its axis, the far horn shows only the far left cheek: 100 % of its straight lines land there.

So a matching far panel would change nothing visible in B1, apart from possible faint spill. The near/far contrast the finding describes cannot be seen from this seat.

In T2 a matching far panel would show only a little: about 6 % of the far horn's mouth and a strip about 14 px wide.

This is a consistency note at most, not a fix.

verified.recommendation_check:
Keep the overall shape: the lane's option (1) against the black horn, with at most two extra tests. I would change these points.

1. **Drop F7 as a reason.** From B1 the far bay's back is hidden behind its right upright, and the far horn shows only its left cheek. Lighting both bays alike is fine as consistency, but it does not change the B1 picture. In T2 it shows only as a sliver.

2. **T1's expected numbers are guesses.** They come from a strip model that does not match the rendered strip: on the felt cheek the render peaks at z 2.40, not just under the lip.
   - Judge T1 by lemon, not by the share above L* 5. Back plus cheek is only 66.6 % of the mouth, so 70-75 % above L* 5 would count the dim olive ceiling band as lemon.
   - Use C* >= 20 and hue 85-115: the mouth is 29.7 % lemon now in w1 and 31.4 % in b160.
   - Also use the 168 px thumbnail and the studio front's horn (L* 52.7, C* 55.3, h 97).
   - Use one baseline: the lane's 32 % is a box share, which includes about 7 % lit pixels outside the mouth.
   - T1 will carry b160's gold streaks along the horn's lower-left rim. They are grazing reflections of the strip-lit niche (R up to about 30 %), and the owner may read them as a render fault.

3. **Render the fallback first.** It is the likely final and nobody has seen it: w1 with the speaker 2 cm right and 5 cm deeper, as a crop, before T2.
   - Use w1 rather than b160 for it: no streaks and no lit cheek top.
   - My numbers: back 44 %, cheek 26 %, ceiling 12 %.
   - The nudge also halves the lit panel seen beside the horn (6.0k to 2.9k px), so the display-case read is less. The cost is more felt seen directly: the gap left of the cabinet goes from 34 to 54 px.
   - Confirm the niche depth before moving the speaker back.
   - Do not add the 1.55 m eye: it pushes the drinks' bases out of the frame.

4. **T2 needs two notes.**
   - The gain comes as much from stepping back to y 2.9 as from the angle. Straight on but still on the bar's seat line (y 3.5), the ceiling band stays at about 13 %.
   - The lit w1 panel still shows directly, as an L-shaped glow under and right of the horn: about 5.9k px, the same as B1's 6.0k.

**Owner sentence.** As written it has three problems:
- It leaves out the black top edge, which is the ceiling: 15 % of the mouth.
- It says "only", but the nudge enlarges the lemon part with no new light.
- It states "look like a display case" before anyone has seen T1, which breaks "say only what you saw".

Suggested wording: "The horn is clear, so from this seat its left side and top edge look straight through to the black felt on the niche's side wall and ceiling; only the part in front of the lit back shows lemon. Setting the speaker a little deeper and to the right makes that lemon part bigger. Making nearly all of it lemon would need the niche's walls lit too, or a seat almost straight in front of the speaker and further back, and I'll show you each as a picture before you choose."

The pictures are zones-mine-on-tests.png, horn-gamma-4.png, ov2-b400.png, farbay-fixed7.png, panel-halo-B1-T2.png and streaks-vs-grazing.png. The scripts are vtrace.py, vstraight.py, direct2.py and cheekprof.py.
